value_or_null.description: Retrospective single-center cohort, almost all prescribed aspirin, no suitable randomized or balanced alternative-agent/no-prophylaxis comparison. Residual VTE/bleeding burden does not isolate causal aspirin inefficacy/harm, DOAC superiority or a new prescription. Authors unacceptable-risk/change-strategy wording is attributed interpretation, not adopted judgment.

356screened/250included/106excluded, including13earlydeaths and22lostfollowup with<3months. Minimum3monthfollowup excludes early outcomes and can bias incidence/survival. Tertiary referral population, mostly intermediate/highrisk with high-dose steroids/thalidomide, not general low-risk or modern lenalidomide cohorts.

Source says248patients98.6%ASA, but248/250=99.2%;discussion98.9%ASA/1.1%apixaban also differs from2/250initialapixaban. Preserve all literals and arithmetic qualification without rewriting the source or inferring another denominator. FourASA-to-apixaban switches are not four additional baseline patients.

37labeledVTE include31lower-extremity events,3PE,2superficialvein and1temporalveinthrombosis; do not silently describe all37 as conventional objectively confirmed DVT/PE. Four thrombotic events were incidentally detected, no routine screening; VTE/arterial/bleeding overlap not separately summed as unique patients.

20VTEinfirst6months,8inmonths7-12,9after12months total37/25014.8%. Medianfollowup19months withrange3-74 is not a fixed19monthrisk window or patient-time incidence rate; no eventCI or exact per-patienttime supplied. KM-derived cumulative incidence differs from death-competing CIF; death not stated as competing event.

Fourteen majorbleeding events occurred in12patients;4.8%=12/250, not14/250. ElevenCRNMpatients include2also withmajorbleed history, so14+11or12+11 cannot be independent unique bleeding patients. Source9MBpatients onASA and3therapeuticanticoagulants describes patients/exposures, not necessarily14event allocations. No causal ASA-attributable bleeding risk established.

CRNM paragraph says allassociatedwithlow-doseASA while4patients also ontherapeuticFXainhibitorsforVTE; concomitant exposure/timing unclear. Three fatalhemorrhages associatedwithASA areobservedassociations,notattributionsolelytoASA. Post-VTEtherapeuticanticoagulation differsfromprimaryprophylaxis and affectsbleeding interpretation.

PRISM narrative says167assessed,2low/133intermediate/32high;Table2says2/122/32 totaling156, with1.3/78.2/20.5percent. Abstract/bodylowrisk2(.5%) is inconsistent with either. Do not silently change122to133 or assign one denominator to all ROC/curve results. This unresolved source inconsistency needs original data/supplement.

SAVEDTable2low3/2501.2%,high247/25098.8%,bodyhigh99.5%; preserve difference. Very small low-risk groups in all scores limit validation, lack of statistical separation is not universal model invalidity or equal patient risk.

IMPEDEbodyAUC61.5%CI48.8%-0.74% has malformed units;Figure2prints61.5%CI48.8-74.3 and is retained separately, no silent repair. ROCIMPEDEP.09 is distinct fromTable2P.41/Figure1logrank.4154. SAVEDROC.94,Table.999,logrank.6108 andPRISMROC.75/.73,Table.93,12monthlogrank.8459 remain test/time-specific, not interchangeable positive findings.

ROC AUC discrimination is not calibration, prospective clinical utility or prevention benefit. AllFigure2AUC CIs include chance50%. Cohen kappa.185CI.007-.36 is interscore agreement, not model discrimination or clinical efficacy. Multivariate score-item results reside in unchecked supplement and cannot supply verified adjusted aspirin effects.

MedianOS62months/64deaths,Figure3VTE37with10deaths versusnoVTE213with54deaths,logrankP.088. Nonsignificance does not confirm VTE has no impact or rule out clinically meaningful harm. No time-dependent VTE model or confounder adjustment of this survival contrast described; early-death exclusion and ever-VTE grouping may bias interpretation. Fourteendeathcausesunknown, fatalPEcannotberuledout accordingtoauthors.
